purpose: Authoritative proof-suitability matrix for all 123 Wave B J4E/J4F scenarios — mechanically derived from real pytest collection and AST-based source inspection of every test function body (never from file names, comments, or self-declared manifest status).
methodology: For each scenario's mapped pytest node, the test function body was parsed via ast.walk and scanned for calls to real production functions (module.build_*, module.process_*, module.persist_*, compute_postmortem(), process_current_report(), close_paper_trade(), pg_conn.execute(), etc. = BEHAVIOURAL) versus structural-only markers (inspect.getsource, hasattr(module,...), _require_orchestrator() with no further assertion, importlib.util.find_spec = STRUCTURAL). A scenario whose own node is structural but has a real companion test (from the Wave B closure PostgreSQL/async test files) proving the SAME underlying invariant is marked MIXED_WITH_BEHAVIOURAL_COMPANION/ADEQUATE. A scenario with neither is marked STRUCTURAL_SUFFICIENT/REQUIRES_COMPANION — an HONEST, NOT-YET-CLOSED gap, disclosed rather than silently treated as adequate.
honest_disclosure: 43 of 123 scenarios are marked REQUIRES_COMPANION — their mapped node is structural-only (existence/signature/source-string checks) and no genuine behavioural/async/real-PostgreSQL companion test currently proves the same runtime invariant. This is NOT claimed as closed. Converting all 43 into adequate proof was not completed in this closure pass given realistic time constraints; the 27 companion tests added in this arc (Sections 8A-8I, 8K) closed the highest-priority runtime invariants (endpoint provenance, reconciliation state machine, settlement, market-local date, five-phase boundary, worker lifecycle, close-to-outbox atomicity, global claim/lease, supersession/coexistence, reset/cross-user isolation) but did not exhaustively convert every one of the 123 mapped nodes.
